name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateTextScroll
summary: 1984-byte state machine on window+0x5FF that scrolls/types the current message line, plays SEs, moves the camera focus and rebuilds model parts; the body is damaged (halt_baddata, overlapping instructions) and mixes text-window with battle unit-model work, so no single class fits.
evidence: Re-checked against the now-named neighbours: callees read Sound_PlaySeById, BattleScene_GetUnitModelVariant, Model_SetupPartsFromTable, Battle_UnitList_SetActorsFloatParam and Camera_SetFocusOffsetAndBlend, i.e. camera plus battle unit-model work sits next to the text scrolling, so a plain message-window text scroll stays unproven; still no callers.

name: maybe_Battle_ActorAction_SpawnImpactEffects
summary: Action branch of a battle actor: resolves the action row (func_0063FD24(dm, actor+0x497)), compares the actor class chain with g_enemyBattleActorNizuzerufaClass, clears flag 0x2000 / sets actor+0x4E1 and drives the action state at actor+0x623. The jump table and part of the body are lost, so the 'impact effects' reading only covers the tail.
evidence: Game_GetDataManager plus func_0063FD24 (action rows) and the explicit class compare with g_enemyBattleActorNizuzerufaClass are visible, but the effect-spawn part sits behind halt_baddata and the function has no callers.

name: Ui_RebuildParts
signature: void Ui_RebuildParts(Window* window, const u8* layoutDesc, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Rebuilds a composite window's optional child parts: frees the old part blocks at +0xCC/+0xD0/+0xD4 and recreates each one from the layout descriptor with its own sub-window constructor (panel message, monster book, stamp book, present window), then fills the new parts from the descriptor.
evidence: Named caller Ui_SmithMenu_RefreshParts calls it exactly when the smith layout changes, and every branch is the same pattern: release the old block, Mem_AllocAligned_2 a fixed size, run the type-specific ctor (Ui_PanelMessageWindow_CtorEx, Ui_MonsterBookWindow_Ctor, Ui_StampBookWindow_Ctor, Ui_PresentWindow_Ctor). The 'parts' wording now describes the observed per-field rebuild.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteNode_EmitBurst
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SpriteNode_EmitBurst(SpriteNode* node, const float* position, u32 effectId)
summary: Builds a 0x68-byte effect descriptor from the sprite node (handle at node+4, scale f_304, effect handle f_300) and spawns a burst effect in front of the camera; two halt_baddata sites truncate the control flow, so the trigger condition is unknown.
evidence: Ui_ResolveObjectHandle at the top and Field_HandleIsValid on node->childObject are the only named anchors; the descriptor + Os_GetGameWork path survives but the first branch is bad instruction data.

name: maybe_Actor_ApplyModelStateEffect
signature: void maybe_Actor_ApplyModelStateEffect(void* actor, u32 effectWord, u32 arg3, u32 flags)
summary: Applies an effect/state word to an actor's attached model: reads the effect-target record (Battle_Action_SelectEffectTarget), picks the model or target anchor, runs the attribute evaluator maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_ApplyAttribute, plays the 8-way direction animation, or sends event commands 0/1 to the actor's event state, then releases the unit handle.
evidence: The caller list is field/actor code (Actor_PlayShakeAnim, Field_Action_PitfallSetState, Field_Action_OpenDoor, Field_Action_WalkStartToTarget, ActorAction_BeginMove), the caller 'mask' is forwarded straight into maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_ApplyAttribute(flags) as an attribute selector, and the tail is Event_OnTriggerCommand plus Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation. The old name claimed a battle-only part mask the body does not contain.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteNode_EmitBurstOnEvent
summary: Event handler of a sprite node: events 4/5 latch the target handle/alpha, event 1 computes the direction from the camera to the node and spawns a burst with SE 0xFD through Monster_NotifyCommand20; the meaning of the event ids is still unidentified.
evidence: Only Os_GetGameWork and Monster_NotifyCommand20 are named; the camera-to-node vector maths is clear but event ids 1/4/5 and the sprite-node class remain guesses.

name: maybe_Text_BuildRowDescriptor
signature: void maybe_Text_BuildRowDescriptor(void* outRow, u32 x, u32 y, u32 flags)
summary: Builds a 0x58-byte text-row descriptor: allocates two temporary 0xB190 layout/status blocks (vtable g_vtableUiPartyStatus), runs Text_ApplyRowStyle on them, frees them and copies the resulting descriptor into the caller's buffer. Nothing is drawn, so the old 'Text_DrawComplex' was misleading.
evidence: The body ends in std_memcpy(out, &resultBuffer, 0x58) and both temporary objects are released through their vtable slot +4 right after Text_ApplyRowStyle, which is a builder, not a draw; consumers are Ui_StatusPanel_ChangeMember and Ui_SakusenWindow_BuildMessageArgs. Buffer contents/ownership are still only partly decoded.

name: Field_Scene_FindObjectValueById
summary: Resolves an object id to an actor handle via Actor_GetModelHandleById and, when that misses, walks the scene object list for the script-gadget class (g_scriptGadgetActorClassRecord) whose f_88 equals the id, returning its secondary word; used by the gadget list and event actor-slot lookups.
evidence: Three named callers (Field_GadgetList_FindOrAddByHandle, Event_GetOrAddActorSlot, Field_FindObjectByMode) all use it as an id-to-object/handle resolve, and the class compare plus f_88 equality make the fallback path explicit.

name: maybe_Battle_TextWindow_UpdateTargetMarker
summary: Per-frame update of a text panel that follows a target actor: validates the handle at +0x25C, reads the target's position/rotation, pushes position and matrix into the panel and hides the panel when the handle is lost. The single caller is a field gimmick selection cursor, so the 'Battle_' prefix is only the neighbour cluster.
evidence: Named callees Battle_TextWindow_UpdateVisibility/Alt, Model_ApplyMotionResource and Ui_GetCore plus the g_actorAttachGadgetHandleMap validation and the latch byte at +600 fit the body, but the only caller is maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateSelectionCursor, which contradicts a battle-window-only role.

name: maybe_Actor_ApplyChangedStateMessages
signature: void maybe_Actor_ApplyChangedStateMessages(void* group, const u8* changeFlags, void* actor, u32 altTable)
summary: Walks a 28-entry change-flag table (2 bytes per entry, alt table selected by the last argument) and, for every changed part, queues the matching battle message or equipment-slot message (slots 0x20..0x22, 2..0x12, 0x112) and creates the appearance effect from the part or item record when the battle work is in 3D mode.
evidence: The whole body is a switch over indices 0..0x1B calling maybe_Actor_QueueEquipmentMessage(group, slot, actor) and Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry with message ids 0x56/0x27/0x44, gated by paramTable[i*2 + (flags!=0) + 0x1A]. Nothing attaches a set to a party group, so 'FieldParty_ApplyAttachmentSet' was wrong; with 187 callers in field, battle and UI code it is a generic per-actor 'state changed' notifier.

name: Ui_ReleaseGfxResources
summary: Tears a composite window down: lazily creates the 0x7C message-window helper at +0x98, notifies and frees the four renderer resources at +0xCC/+0xD0/+0xD4/+0xD8 and clears the shared handle at +0x94, passing resource kinds 0/8/0xF/9 to the notify callback.
evidence: A clean four-branch teardown: each branch notifies func_002171FC(self, kind, data) and then frees its block (Menu_TalkParty_ReleasePanel / func_003B7E0C / Ui_UpdateWindowParts / Ui_DestroyRootSingleton); the resource-release reading matches every branch, and the lazy Ui_MessageWindow_Ctor at +0x98 is the only creation.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_SpawnItemEffect
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_SpawnItemEffect(void* self, void* anchorA, void* anchorB)
summary: Spawns a pickup effect at the midpoint of two anchors (positions averaged with 0.5, plus a 0.65 height offset) using the effect id taken from Item_LookupRecord; both anchor arguments are phantom Ghidra parameters, so the owning gimmick class is unproven.
evidence: Item_LookupRecord and Effect_FindOrCreateInstance are named, but the body reads arg2->halfExtentY / arg3->f_9c on invented parameters and carries a type-propagation warning, so the 'item effect at anchor midpoint' reading is only structural.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleTargetMarker_CreateFromModelRecord
summary: Initialises an effect-anchor set from a model record (func_0063DF9C(dm, id)): stores the record's f_C4 as the effect type and, for each 0x18-byte marker record, resolves the unit slot and creates the effect instance at the slot position.
evidence: Named callers now span Battle_Ui_UpdateStateMachine, Text_MessageWindow_UpdateAnchors, Text3D_UpdateBillboardTransform and Camera_StartEventPath, which is too broad for a battle target marker; the 0x18-byte record loop and the effect creation are clear, the owner class is not.

name: Field_Gimmick_SpawnOrientedEffect
signature: void Field_Gimmick_SpawnOrientedEffect(FieldGimmick* self, int arg2, EffectAnchor* anchor)
summary: Builds an orthonormal frame from the anchor rotation (axis offsets 0.65 and 0.2) and spawns the effect oriented along that frame at the anchor position.
evidence: The body is entirely the frame construction (constants 3F266666 = 0.65 and 3E4CCCCD = 0.2 applied to anchor->halfExtent/maybe_quat fields) feeding Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and Os_GetGameWork; the same anchor layout appears in the sibling 0x005DE518, so 'oriented effect spawn' is directly readable.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowAndStoreArgsB
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowAndStoreArgsB(void* gimmick, void* ctx, int* arg3, int* args)
summary: Sibling of 0x005E3FE0: clears the gimmick side-state flags, places a row with Ui_ObjectList_SwapOrder, sets the row asset id and copies the 0x11-byte argument block into the state record.
evidence: Same named callee set as 0x005E3FE0 (Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId, Ui_ObjectList_SwapOrder, std_memcpy, Field_Gimmick_ReleaseValidHandles) and the same 0x11-byte block copy; the 'B' suffix only records that it is the second of the pair and there are no callers.

name: Ui_PostEvent0E
summary: Writes the value into the save work via func_00612550(work+0x24A98, value) and then posts event 0x0E with that byte to the UI core's active object, only when the game work and the active object exist.
evidence: All call targets are now named (Os_GetGameWork, Ui_GetCore, Game_GetWork) and the event id 0x0E plus the single-byte payload are read straight from the body (func_002171FC(activeObject, 0xe, eventData)).

name: maybe_Actor_DispatchActionByType
signature: void maybe_Actor_DispatchActionByType(int actorIndex, int actionType, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Resolves event-actor slot actorIndex (optional for action types 5, 0xB-0xF, 0x11 and 0x12), validates its handle and forwards both slot handles plus the action type to Ui_Overlay_ResolveSlotSprite.
evidence: Ui_Overlay_ResolveSlotSprite and Os_GetGameWork are named, but there are no callers and the slot handles arrive in damaged r6/r7 registers, so 'dispatch by type' remains a description of the type test rather than a proven method.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_CreateEffectOnCommand
summary: Command handler of a small widget: command 0x29 builds a default descriptor and creates effect instance 0x689, storing the handle at +0x220; every other command is forwarded to the children.
evidence: Effect_FindOrCreateInstance(..., 0x689, ...) and Field_SceneNode_ForwardCommandToChildren are named and the +0x220 store is explicit, but the owner is known only as a scene node/widget, so the prefix stays open.

name: maybe_Battle_ReleaseUnitHandle
summary: Drops the weak handle at +0x39C: notifies the bound object through vtable +0xB4 when its flag word has 0x20000010 set, clears +0x395, resets the handle to the invalid value and drops the UI core's cached object.
evidence: The handle decode against g_actorAttachGadgetHandleMap and the vtable +0xB4 notification are clear, but the rebuilt sentinel comes from damaged registers and the two named callers (Ui_Overlay_UpdateMarkerTrail, 0x0023B2F0) do not pin the owning class.

name: maybe_Field_SetEventTalkAttrByte
summary: Copies one talk/NPC attribute byte (Field_NpcEntry_GetTalkAttrByte(attrId)) into event state +0x94C, storing 0xFF when the attribute id is 0x10 or larger. The old 'time zone' wording had no support in the body.
evidence: The body is only the attribute query plus the < 0x10 clamp into eventState->f_94C; there is no zone/id table and no caller, so only the 'writes a talk-attribute byte into event state' part is safe.

name: maybe_Ui_RegisterActorVariant
signature: uint32_t maybe_Ui_RegisterActorVariant(UiActorHolder* holder, UiActor* actor, uint32_t extra, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Registers an actor in a UI actor slot: writes the actor handle to holder+0xC, fills +0xD/+0xE, bumps the use count at +0x10, binds the slot with Ui_ActorSlot_BindActor and decrements the pending count at +0xF.
evidence: 35 callers are almost all field object, talk-balloon and object-sprite constructors, which supports a slot-registration helper, but r6/r8 arrive damaged and the 'variant' wording is still unsupported by any field.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_Register
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_Register(FieldSceneObject* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Marks a field scene object registered (f_264) and, when it is visible/enabled and has been bound, hands the current target object to the effect part (Gfx_EffectPart_SetTargetObject) and clears the pending flag.
evidence: Gfx_EffectPart_SetTargetObject and Os_GetGameWork are the only named anchors and r6 is damaged; callers are NPC cursor/talk-range helpers, so 'Register' summarises the flag write rather than a proven object method.

name: maybe_Ui_LayoutGroup_Refresh
summary: 28-byte entry that refreshes the owner actor (0x001835AC) and then continues into the shared 16-entry layout-table/builder code at 0x001B7A54; the decompiler inlines the same body, so only the entry differs from its sibling.
evidence: The function is 28 bytes and ends exactly at 0x001B7A54, whose 780-byte body is reproduced identically here - this is an alternate entry into the builder, not an independent refresh routine, which also explains the 'layout group' wording.

name: maybe_Ui_LayoutGroup_Build
summary: Builds the shared 16-slot layout table once and creates or moves the owner actor's entry from its f_9C/f_A0/f_A4 position (via Math_Curve_EvaluatePoint and Field_Actor_GetModelScaleVector), carrying the actor/model scale.
evidence: Sibling 0x001B7A38 is a 28-byte alternate entry into this body; the only caller is maybe_Actor_ReleaseBoundsCheck and the callee Field_Actor_GetModelScaleVector fits the position-entry reading, but 'Ui_LayoutGroup' itself is still unverified.

name: Field_Action_CreateMoveEffect
summary: Creates the movement effect for a field action: builds a default descriptor, spawns effect 0x4F1 through the world effect manager and stores the handle in action->stepProgress, where Field_Action_StopMoveEffect later releases it.
evidence: The create/stop pair is now closed: this function stores action->stepProgress and 0x00302AE0 (Field_Action_StopMoveEffect) releases exactly that handle via Effect_ReleaseHandle(work->0x60, action->stepProgress, 0). Renamed from 'CreateWalkEffect' to the neutral 'Move' because nothing in the body identifies walking.

name: maybe_Ui_Component_FindAndSetFlags
summary: Looks the current scene object's handle (scene+0x20) up in the actor-attach handle map, walks its class chain to g_uiComponentClass and calls vtable +0xB8 with an invalid handle and 0; the 'set flags' half of the old name is unverified.
evidence: Handle-map lookup, class-chain walk and vtable +0xB8 are clear, but the two arguments actually passed (invalid handle, 0) look like a reset/clear rather than setting flags; no callers, and in_r3 plus the 0xFFFFF800 OR show damaged registers.

name: maybe_Gfx_Effect_CreateByIdFromObject
signature: u32 maybe_Gfx_Effect_CreateByIdFromObject(UiObject* self, u32 id, int variant)
summary: Searches the object's baked resource id table (u16 ids, 4-byte stride, table at ownerEffect->f_74) for the requested id and, on a hit, creates the corresponding effect instance through Effect_FindOrCreateInstance.
evidence: The 18 named callers are SmithMenu/StatusPanel/TextBuilder detail refreshes, consistent with 'create the effect belonging to this UI object', and the id-table scan is explicit; the object hierarchy (ownerEffect->f_74/f_4C) is still unmapped, so the class stays open.

name: maybe_Ui_HandleSet_DtorLarge
summary: Destructor that releases the handle set at +0x84 (Pack_ReleaseHandle), stamps the three vtables at -0x40/-0x60/-0x80 and returns this-0x84; the class label is inferred only from the stamped vtable globals.
evidence: Only callee is Pack_ReleaseHandle, there are no callers, and the adjusted return pointer (this-0x84) plus three vtable stamps are the entire evidence for the class.

name: Ui_ToggleButton_Ctor
summary: Small widget constructor: Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs g_uiToggleButtonVtable and ORs the default state/mask word at +0x4C; called from Ui_DungeonBattleWindow_Ctor to build a child widget.
evidence: The installed vtable is the binary symbol g_uiToggleButtonVtable, so the class label comes from the game, not from the caller; Ui_Object_CtorBase immediately before the vtable store confirms it is a constructor.

name: maybe_Container_AddMaskedEntry08
signature: void maybe_Container_AddMaskedEntry08(void* owner, const MaskedEntry* entry)
summary: Allocates a 0x10-byte intrusive-list node from the owner's heap, stores the masked id (entry+4 & 0x7FF) and links it into the list at owner+8; one of four identical siblings differing only in destination list.
evidence: Body is byte-identical to 0x00451714/0x00451790/0x0045180C; the named caller Ui_Part_BindSlotsToLayout shows these are the per-slot lists, but what a node means (and why the id is masked) is not decoded.

name: maybe_Container_AddMaskedEntry20
signature: void maybe_Container_AddMaskedEntry20(void* owner, const MaskedEntry* entry)
summary: Same masked-id append as 0x00451540 but into the intrusive list at owner+0x20; identical 0x10-byte node layout and 0x7FF mask.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x00451540 apart from the destination list and mask literal; no callers, so only the structural reading is available.

name: maybe_Container_AddMaskedEntry14
signature: void maybe_Container_AddMaskedEntry14(void* owner, const MaskedEntry* entry)
summary: Same masked-id append as 0x00451540 but into the intrusive list at owner+0x14; called from Gfx_SpriteNode_SetPosition, which is consistent with per-feature node lists on one owner.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x00451540 apart from the destination list and mask literal; the one named caller (Gfx_SpriteNode_SetPosition) does not explain the entry meaning.

name: maybe_Container_AddMaskedEntry2C
signature: void maybe_Container_AddMaskedEntry2C(void* owner, const MaskedEntry* entry)
summary: Same masked-id append as 0x00451540 but into the intrusive list at owner+0x2C; called from Ui_Part_BindSlotsToLayout together with the +8 sibling.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x00451540 apart from the destination list and mask literal; Ui_Part_BindSlotsToLayout calls both this and 0x00451540, so they are sibling per-slot lists.

name: maybe_Ui_Pane_SetScrollRect
summary: Copies the rect at self+0x34/+0x38 into the render object's +0x138/+0x13C and, when the draw context has no such rect queued, requests a redraw; the 'scroll rect' wording is a reading of the field pair, not proof.
evidence: Ui_GetCore plus the dirty-rect query func_006282D0 survive, but the rectangle construction is garbled (garbled 0xFFFFF800 words) and the function has no callers.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_InitMemberSlotArray
summary: Object initialiser: stores the caller's vtable in word 0, masks four handle words to the invalid handle and default-constructs three 0xC0-byte member blocks with element ctor 0x0030BE18; the 'gimmick member slot array' label is inferred from the field layout only.
evidence: std_ConstructArray(self+5, 0x0030BE18, 0xC0, 3) is clear, but the vtable arrives in an undeclared register, there are no callers and no field proves a gimmick link.

name: maybe_Battle_Popup3D_UpdateRootEx
summary: 22-byte alternate entry inside the 3D battle popup update: the constructor path initialises the gauge-bar fields and vtable, the other path picks the first free popup slot at +0x11C, applies the slide offset and finishes through vtable +0x2C.
evidence: The address 0x002E8B7E is not 4-byte aligned and lies inside the neighbouring routine, and the decompiler merges two entries with unaff_ registers, so only the entry role is known; there are no callers or named callees.

name: Ui_FillColorFromActor
summary: Fills a UI colour record (colour id word plus RGBA) from the actor's colour table, defaulting to opaque white when no actor or handle is supplied.
evidence: Three named UI callers (Ui_Window_SetTextById, Ui_TextTable_FindRecord, Ui_ProfileWindow_UpdateDetails) plus the white-default initialisation and the func_0064A4C8 colour-id read followed by func_00672318(out+1, actor+0x14C) make the colour-fill role explicit.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawFogPass
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawFogPass(Gfx_ModelInstance* instance, int cmdList, unsigned arg3, int* state, int* mode)
summary: Model-instance draw pass chosen by Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawPassDispatcher: builds a 3x4 texture-matrix block (texel scales 0x3E600000/0x3F700000), binds the texture and emits the parts.
evidence: The only caller is the pass dispatcher and every callee is a texture-matrix/bind/emit helper; no fog register, fog constant or state change appears in the body, so which of the three near-identical passes this is remains open.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawMultiStatePass
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawMultiStatePass(Gfx_ModelInstance* instance, int cmdList, unsigned arg3, int* state, int* mode)
summary: Model-instance draw pass dispatched by Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawPassDispatcher: same texture-matrix setup as the sibling passes plus an extra colour-state block (Gfx_ModelInstance_ApplyColorState) and per-part texture matrices.
evidence: Single caller is the pass dispatcher; the callee set (ApplyColorState, BindTexture, DrawTexCoordPass, BindTextureAndDraw) shows what differs from the siblings, but no identifying constant names the feature.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawOverrideMaterialPass
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawOverrideMaterialPass(Gfx_ModelInstance* instance, int cmdList, unsigned arg3, int* override, int* mode)
summary: Draws a model instance with an overriding material: builds the matrix block, binds the caller's texture, installs the material GX state and emits parts through Gfx_Pica_EmitDrawElements; the body has instruction overlap at 0x00569E34 and unreachable-block warnings, so the pass identity stays a maybe_.
evidence: Three named callers agree on the role - Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawAllPasses, Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawOverridePass and Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawPassDispatcher - and the body consumes the caller-supplied override/material pointer, but the damaged region was not re-read in assembly, so the name is not promoted.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateSlotEffects
summary: Loops the gimmick's f_1BC slots at stride 0x14, resolves each attached actor through the gadget handle map, tests the actor-group member class and positions/orients the effects through the 0x005DE434.. helpers; what a 'slot' represents is still unidentified.
evidence: Named callees Field_Gimmick_MarkActorsInStateB, Field_Gimmick_PlayVariantReaction, Field_ActorGroup_PlaceMember and Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection plus the stride-0x14 loop bound self->maybe_count1BC fit the body, but there are no callers to confirm the gimmick class.

name: Ui_SpritePart_Update
summary: Per-frame fade/timer update of a UI sprite part: re-resolves and clears the sprite, counts down the blink timer, fades the alpha toward zero and, when finished, hides the owning button and clears the UI list through the 0x10 and 0x58 vtable slots.
evidence: The body is a self-contained fade-out state machine (spriteIndex -1, blinkCountdown, fadeAlpha -= 0x3D088889, isFinished latch) with named callees Ui_Sprite_DrawByName, Ui_TitleWindow_SetButtonVisible and Container_IntrusiveList_ClearAll, matching a sprite-part update.

name: Field_ModelSlotEmitter_InitFromDef
signature: void Field_ModelSlotEmitter_InitFromDef(ModelSlotSet* emitter, int* def, u32 appearanceId, int template)
summary: Seeds a model-slot emitter from a spawn definition and an optional template: builds or copies the 0x84 appearance record (Data_SelectRecordIdByWeight + maybe_Ui_List_BuildRowRecord), resets timers/flags/colours, copies the definition's rotation fields and builds the point path.
evidence: The real constructor Field_ModelSlotEmitter_Ctor (0x004B3374) exists as a sibling and this routine performs the definition-driven initialisation it calls (std_memcpy of the 0x84 appearance block, Path_BuildFromPoints, Gfx_Node_SetEulerRotation, def+0x35..0x39 flag bytes).

name: maybe_Actor_ComputeFacingAngleFromReference
summary: Computes the unsigned angle between a forward vector (Math_QuatToForwardVector of the scene) and the global reference axis g_directionReferenceVector, takes the sign from the cross term, converts it to degrees modulo 360 into self+0x11C and stores two rotated reference vectors alongside.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Field_ObjectSprite_UpdateOwner and the result is written into that caller's object at +0x11C, while the forward vector comes from the scene node at (work+8)->f_48 - no camera pointer is involved, so 'Camera_ComputeAngleFromReference' named the wrong owner.

name: Field_Action_StopMoveEffect
summary: Stops the in-flight movement effect (handle in action->stepProgress, created by 0x003027C8), releases the attached object/SE, restores the actor's animation speed unless keepAnimSpeed == 1 and clears f_276/f_2d4 (plus f_278/f_27c on the full path).
evidence: It releases action->stepProgress through Effect_ReleaseHandle(work->0x60, ...) and clears exactly the fields the run/effect starters set; the create side is the now-named Field_Action_CreateMoveEffect (0x003027C8).

name: maybe_Ui_DungeonHpWindow_LayoutRows
signature: void maybe_Ui_DungeonHpWindow_LayoutRows(UiDungeonHpWindow* self, float* out, int count, u32 arg4, int arg5)
summary: Writes -1.0f into the first three output floats and, for a valid row count, looks a value up through the data manager (func_0063EDD4/func_00640158) and stores it as out[2]; the body is heavily damaged (dead-code heritage, fake game-work init block).
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Ui_DungeonHpWindow_AnimateRows, so the class and the 'row layout' meaning are circular; the data-manager lookup into (work+0x24A98)+count*0x8C+0x5FE4 is the only solid part.

name: Field_Action_ToggleRun
summary: Starts or toggles running for a field action: initialises the horse params, copies the five preset motion floats, tests the target actor's active state, then either takes the continue-check path or calls Field_Action_SetRunState(isRunning) and swaps the actor's speed presets.
evidence: The named callee trio Field_Action_InitHorseParams / Field_Action_SetRunState / Field_Action_Run_CheckCanContinue plus the preset copies and the actor->f_276/f_278/f_2d4 writes make the run-state role explicit.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveSubObject_Ctor
summary: Widget constructor: Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs g_uiGaugeBarWindowVtable, sets the scale/position floats at +0x4C..+0x5C and constructs the embedded animation-ref list at +0x18; a second, dive-flavoured vtable (maybe_g_uiDiveGaugeBarVtable) is stored near that list.
evidence: The outer vtable is g_uiGaugeBarWindowVtable, so this is a gauge-bar window constructor; the 'Dive' part rests only on the inner vtable store at animRefList-0x60 (a suspicious negative offset), so the subtype is not established.

name: Ui_SlotTable_ApplyEntry
summary: Applies the currently selected slot: stores the slot value byte at +2, sets the 2D scene sprite character id through the Field2D sprite set (unless the game mode byte is 2) and resets the selection timer.
evidence: Named callers Ui_SlotTable_Refresh and Ui_SlotTable_UpdateSelection plus the shared self+0x23..0x36 slot array with -1 sentinel across the five SlotTable functions confirm the role; the sprite side is (work+8)->f_88 (Field2D) with Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetCharacterId.

name: Ui_SlotTable_RefreshForSpeaker
summary: Derives the speaker id, rolls the random slot pairs, scans the ten (id, value) pairs for the one matching the current 2D sprite record and selects/applies it, falling back to the stored selection when none matches.
evidence: Calls Ui_SlotTable_RollRandomEntries and Ui_SlotTable_GetSelectedId and then the two sibling helpers, over the same ten-pair table with -1 sentinel and the same speaker comparison against spriteRecord->f_1c.

name: maybe_Model_SecondaryMotion_BuildChains
signature: u32 maybe_Model_SecondaryMotion_BuildChains(void* self, u32 allocTag, void* model)
summary: Rebuilds secondary-motion chains: clears the old buffers (Model_SecondaryMotion_Clear), walks the model nodes and their attribute names, classifies them and allocates/constructs the chain entries.
evidence: 5546-byte body with dozens of bad-instruction and unreachable-block warnings; the named callees (Model_SecondaryMotion_Clear, Mem_AllocAligned, std_ConstructArray, Gfx_ModelInstance_PackSkinningBuffer) fit, but the callers (Ui_UpdateInput, maybe_Field_RunwayEnv_Init) do not, so the chain layout is only partly decoded.

name: maybe_Model_Attach_ApplyFadeRange
summary: Applies a fade range to a model attachment slot: if the slot has no attached mesh yet it creates it with Gfx_Model_AttachGadgetMesh, otherwise it writes the fade fields f_5B4..f_5C4 from the definition and recurses over the child list (f_6B0/f_6B4) calling Model_Attach_SetFadeRange on every child.
evidence: Same field block (f_5B4..f_5C4) and the same child-list recursion as the sibling 0x00222DFC Model_Attach_SetSpinRange, and it tail-recurses through the already named Model_Attach_SetFadeRange - the pair is a spin-range/fade-range setter over the attachment tree. The recovered decompilation has no reliable first argument type.

name: Ui_SlotTable_SelectEntry
signature: void Ui_SlotTable_SelectEntry(void* self, int index, float fade)
summary: Selects a slot table entry by index: stores the index and slot byte, resets the selection timer and re-applies the entry when the fade value is at or below zero; index 0xFF clears the selection.
evidence: Named callers Ui_SlotTable_Refresh/UpdateSelection plus the sibling ApplyEntry and the same ten-pair table make the selection role explicit; the float arrives in s0 (in_s0) which is why Ghidra shows a phantom third parameter.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneObject_CtorB
summary: Second scene-object constructor: installs g_uiCompositeObjectVtable, then chains several sub-object initialisers (Math_QuatMultiply / Camera_BuildProjectionMatrix helpers) and applies scale/angle defaults; only caller is Ui_ScreenController_InitChildren.
evidence: The vtable g_uiCompositeObjectVtable is installed directly, but the sub-object chain (func_001CEDA4 at +1, +0x3C, +0x28) and the mixed model-actor/camera-subsystem vtables leave the concrete type unidentified.

name: maybe_Field_CheckGimmickItemGetFlag
summary: Tail of IsGimmickItemGetTimming: resolves the game-object handle and returns the signed status byte at object+0x2B4 (or 1 when unresolved); the decompiled body is a misdecompiled float/acos tail, so only the assembly describes it.
evidence: The only caller is the named IsGimmickItemGetTimming and the callees are Field_SceneObject_DtorF / Ui_List_IsCursorAtPartyEndRow, i.e. nothing to do with the acos maths the decompiler printed; the role is read from the asm only.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_SetAlphaFromAnimRecord
summary: Applies the animation record's alpha and colour value to the widget (self[0x15]/f_16), clears the dirty byte at +0x35 and calls vtable +0x2C to rebuild; called from field actor and NPC update paths.
evidence: Named callers Field_Actor_UpdateMotionScale and Field_Npc_UpdateAnchor both drive it as an appearance sync, but the record at self[0x17]+0x150 and the field meanings are inferred and one callee is still named Ui_Casino_InitRouletteWheel (likely a misnamed shared helper).

name: Model_Attach_SetSpinRange
signature: void Model_Attach_SetSpinRange(ModelAttachSlot* slot, s32 start, s32 end)
summary: Configures the spin-angle limits in f_5C8..f_5D8 of a model attachment slot (meaningful range when end >= 0, otherwise reset to -1) and recursively propagates them to every child in the f_6B0/f_6B4 intrusive list.
evidence: The twin function 0x00161974 writes the adjacent fade fields f_5B4..f_5C4 with the identical child-list recursion pattern, so this really is the spin-range setter of the same attachment tree; callers Ui_FaceIcon_CreateWidget and Field_SceneNode_CreateMapInstance both configure attachment nodes.

name: maybe_Ui_DungeonHpWindow_AnimateRows
signature: void maybe_Ui_DungeonHpWindow_AnimateRows(UiDungeonHpWindow* self, float* target, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Finds the first bar row (stride 0xBC) that is not yet placed, lays the rows out, copies the target vector into that row's +0x350..+0x358 and starts the tween through Ui_Tween_SetSpeeds.
evidence: The tween start (Ui_Tween_SetSpeeds) and the row scan are clear, but the only caller is Battle_TextWindow_UpdateVisibilityAlt and the layout callee is itself a maybe_ (0x003D4B04), so the 'DungeonHpWindow' class rests on a circular sibling name.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimInterp_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the small 0x30-byte animation-interpolator object: installs g_animInterpVtable, stores the owner at +0xC, sets -1.0f at +0x1C, clears the value words and initialises the embedded sub-object at +4.
evidence: Two other functions (0x0043FFC8 and the sibling at 0x0043FFD4 range) have the same body with only a different vtable, and all of them install g_animInterpVtable / g_animInterpVtableB and call func_002ACF08(obj+4) - a per-class ctor of one shared interpolator base, not a list-entry object.

name: maybe_Ui_DungeonMessageWindow_Ctor
summary: Window constructor: allocates through func_001D8B6C, installs g_uiDungeonMessageWindowVtable, clears the +0x11C..+0x130 fields and chains six sub-object initialisers (component record, action trigger, two dungeon row kinds, credit sub-widget).
evidence: The installed vtable is the symbol g_uiDungeonMessageWindowVtable, which is stronger evidence than the previous 'CompositeWindow_Ctor1' guess; the only caller is Battle_TextWindow_Ctor, so the battle/dungeon message-window relationship is still unexplained.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotTable_AddEntry
signature: void maybe_Ui_SlotTable_AddEntry(void* self, int speakerId, int value, void* slots)
summary: Appends a (speaker, value) pair into the ten 2-byte slots at self+0x23 (0xFF sentinel) and, when the id equals the current 2D sprite character, stores it in +0x40 and applies it through 0x003DA144.
evidence: Same slot array and sentinel logic as 0x003DA8A4/Ui_SlotTable_AddEntryEx, and the callers include field scene-object item/effect model creation, but the body is Thumb-damaged (coprocessor_store, in_* registers) and the owner class is inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotTable_AddEntryEx
signature: void maybe_Ui_SlotTable_AddEntryEx(void* slotTable, unsigned char id, unsigned char value)
summary: Appends an (id, value) pair into the first free of ten 2-byte slots at self+0x23 and, when the id matches the current 2D sprite character, applies the entry; the callers are scenario/event code (SetScenarioWeather, Event_ApplyScenarioJumpSettings) and the sprite side reads the Field2D manager at (work+8)+0x88, so the table feeds the 2D character sprite set.
evidence: The slot scan is undamaged and identical to 0x003D9E1E, but the callers do not fit a UI window: they set scenario weather / event jump settings, and the sprite object comes from the Field2D manager, so the 'Ui_SlotTable' class is questionable even though the operation is clear.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimInterp_CtorB
summary: Constructor of the same 0x30-byte animation-interpolator object: installs g_animInterpVtable, stores the owner, sets -1.0f at +0x1C, initialises the embedded +4 block via func_002ACF08 and then swaps in g_animInterpVtableB.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x002E42D0 apart from the final vtable swap (g_animInterpVtableB), which is why its old 'ChildWindowList' name and the odd caller mix (CameraZoom, CameraChange, Ui_ListWindow_InitDataObjects) existed - it is a shared interpolator ctor, not a child-window list.

name: Field_ActorActionSeq_UpdateAlt
summary: Field actor action-sequence runner (states 0x1A6F..0x1AA5): runs the current 0x64-byte entry at +0x70C, resolves the unit/party slot, plays the SE, queues the actor name popup and advances or ends the sequence; a 3D battle aborts it early through the battle work mode byte.
evidence: The single caller is the named Field_ActorActionSeq_ApplyActorCommand, the state field self[0x882] selects the branch, and the callees are the battle/field party sequence helpers (FieldParty_UpdateStateMachine, Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateActorStep, Battle_QueueActorNamePopup, Sound_PlaySeById, PartyGroup_GetSlotActor). The 'Alt' suffix still marks it as the second of the pair.
